current_state_summary.primary_concern: Sector index at 89 and the Carlos conversation both point the same direction — EV transition is not hypothetical anymore. The question is whether I move inventory before the demand materializes or wait until the signal is undeniable. Waiting costs me the lead time advantage.

threat_assessment.immediate: No immediate threat. $941 monthly surplus, 11.3 months runway, savings stable. The danger this tick is not crisis — it is the temptation to mistake stability for safety. Sector index 89 on launch day for a ride-share service is not a coincidence. That number will not recover on its own.
threat_assessment.horizon_2mo: Carlos Ruiz and other mechanics on Auto Row are actively researching or pursuing EV certification. If Patricia funds those certifications at Regional Auto Group's service department — which the DIRECT_IMPACT traffic strongly implies she intends to — then EV service volume in Millfield grows in the next 60 days. My current inventory does not serve that demand. The gap between what mechanics will need and what I currently stock is going to open up faster than my reorder cycle if I don't get ahead of it.
threat_assessment.horizon_6mo: The ICE-only parts lines I restocked at tick 1 are correct for now but have a degrading shelf life. A sector revenue index that trends below 85 starts compressing my wholesale margins. The mechanics who survive the transition will be EV-capable; the ones who don't retrain will see fewer cars. Either way, my customer base is bifurcating. In six months I need to know which half I'm serving — and I want to be serving both halves, not caught between them.

actions.description: Place a starter EV parts order — a small, deliberate test position. Based on what Carlos told me last tick: 12V auxiliary battery systems, EV-rated brake fluid (DOT 4 LV spec), high-voltage insulated gloves and PPE, and thermal management coolant for battery packs. Target total outlay under $1,200 at cost. One to two units of each SKU — not a bet, a probe. Identify one supplier from my tick 2 research who distributes to independent shops without requiring OEM dealer account status.
actions.rationale: Carlos named specific categories. He did not speculate — he told me what his shop is going to need based on certifications he is already pursuing. That is the most direct demand signal a supplier can receive. I am not ordering on a hunch; I am ordering on a customer conversation with a forward-leaning mechanic who has been right about the direction of his own work. A $1,200 test position that sits on the shelf is an education. A $1,200 position that sells inside 45 days tells me to triple down. Either outcome is worth having.
actions.timeline: This week — place the order by end of week so stock arrives before Carlos finishes whatever certification pathway he is on.
actions.expected_outcome: Establish a first EV-adjacent SKU presence in the store. If Carlos or another mechanic buys any of it within 30 days, I scale. If it sits, I have learned something true about timing and I have not lost the business on a small position.

actions.description: Call Carlos Ruiz this week — a short follow-up to our tick 2 conversation. The question I want answered: did anything happen this week that moved his EV certification forward? Has he heard anything from his shop's supplier side about EV parts availability? I am not fishing for Patricia's internal decisions — I am asking Carlos what is happening with Carlos, because Carlos is my customer and that is a normal thing to track.
actions.rationale: The DIRECT_IMPACT messages I have been receiving suggest Patricia is moving fast toward a service department EV strategy. I did not hear that from Carlos — I heard it through other channels. But I can hear from Carlos what the ground-level reality looks like. If he tells me he walked into a meeting with Patricia's team this week, I know the institutional direction and the mechanic direction are aligning. If he says nothing happened, I know there is a lag between strategy and execution that gives me more time. Either answer is useful. The call costs nothing and keeps the relationship warm.
actions.timeline: This week, within the next 3 business days.
actions.expected_outcome: Updated read on Carlos's EV timeline and any signal about Regional Auto Group's service department direction. Maintain the relationship as a peer information exchange, not a one-time conversation.

actions.description: Apply for Maria Santos's $5,000 small business grant. Research the eligibility window, application requirements, and framing this week. Submit the application before end of week. The application narrative: auto parts business in active inventory transition to serve an evolving mechanic customer base, adding EV-adjacent product lines in response to documented local demand shift. The grant funds the EV parts pilot directly — it is a legitimate and accurate framing.
actions.rationale: I noted this at tick 2 and did not execute on it because I was focused on the Carlos conversation. That was the right call for tick 2. Now I need to follow through. Maria's program is real — Patricia attended her town hall, which means the political will and the funding are both live. $5,000 in non-dilutive capital is 1.3 months of expenses. It does not reduce my savings. It does not increase my debt. It specifically funds the EV parts test I am already planning to run. There is no cost to applying and a meaningful upside if awarded. Every week I delay is a week closer to the window closing or the funds being allocated.
actions.timeline: Research and submit this week. Do not wait for the Carlos call outcome — the grant application does not depend on it.
actions.expected_outcome: Application submitted. If awarded within 30 days, $5,000 added to working capital designated for EV inventory expansion. If not awarded, I have lost a few hours and learned something about the program's criteria.

actions.description: Audit my current supplier list for EV parts capability. Call or email two of my primary ICE parts distributors this week and ask directly: do they carry EV-rated brake fluid, auxiliary 12V battery systems, or high-voltage PPE? If yes, I can consolidate EV parts purchasing with existing relationships and existing net terms. If no, I need a dedicated EV supplier account, and I should open one now while I have time to negotiate terms rather than scrambling when demand arrives.
actions.rationale: I spent tick 2 doing desktop research on the EV supply chain. Now I need to convert that research into actual supplier relationships. The worst outcome is reaching the point where mechanics need parts and I do not have an account open with a supplier who carries them. Account setup, net terms negotiation, and minimum order thresholds take time. Getting that infrastructure in place now, before the orders are urgent, is the kind of lead-time advantage that a big box store cannot replicate. They have the SKUs but they do not have my supplier flexibility or my ability to special-order within 24 hours for a known mechanic account.
actions.timeline: This week — two calls or emails, straightforward question, no capital commitment yet.
actions.expected_outcome: Clear map of which existing suppliers carry EV lines and which do not. Either I have EV supplier coverage through existing relationships, or I have identified the gap and can open a new account with a specialized EV parts distributor before the demand is pressing.

actions.description: Review the past two ticks of order patterns across my active mechanic accounts. Flag any customers whose order volume is tapering — even slightly — versus those whose volume is holding steady or growing. This is not an intervention; it is a read. I want to know, before I hear it from the customer, whether anyone is pulling back on ICE parts in a way that suggests they are already shifting their business mix.
actions.rationale: The sector index is 89. That number is an aggregate — it does not tell me which specific accounts are changing. My own order data will. If Marcus at Eastside Auto ordered 40% less brake hardware this month than last month, that is a signal I need to read before I interpret it as random variation. The mechanics who are successfully transitioning to EV will change their parts mix first. I want to see that change coming in my own sales data, not discover it when an account goes quiet. This also tells me which customers to invest more relationship time in versus which are already drifting.
actions.timeline: This week — a few hours reviewing the past 60 days of account order data. No capital, no external contact needed.
actions.expected_outcome: A clear picture of which accounts are stable, which are growing, and which are quietly tapering. Informs where I focus relationship attention and which ICE-only lines to stop restocking aggressively.

decisions.ev_inventory_pilot: proceed — small test position, under $1,200, informed by Carlos conversation
decisions.grant_application: execute this tick — no more deferral
decisions.supplier_audit: proceed — infrastructure move, no capital required
decisions.carlos_follow_up: yes — relationship maintenance plus information update
decisions.major_capital_reallocation: not yet — signals are strong but not confirmed enough to make a large bet; stay lean and fast-turning
decisions.roboride_response: indirect — sector index 89 on launch day means ride-share is already suppressing auto sector revenue. I do not change my strategy in response to RoboRide directly; I change it in response to what it does to mechanic demand over the next 60 days

internal_monologue: I have been telling myself I am watching carefully, and I have been — but the Carlos conversation last tick was not just intelligence gathering, it was a purchase order in disguise, and I have been slow to fill it. He told me exactly what his shop is going to need. I need to have it on the shelf before he finishes his certification, not after. The sector index at 89 on the same day a ride-share service goes live in Millfield is not two separate data points — it is one signal that says the auto sector here is already absorbing the shock, and the mechanics who adapt fastest will be the ones still buying from me in three years. I am not panicking, and I am not waiting — I am placing a small, deliberate bet on a customer conversation I know was real.
archetype_self_assessment: Pragmatist crossing the line into adapter. The EV parts order is not pragmatism inside my existing domain — it is a new domain, a small one, provisionally entered. The grant application is me asking for help, which I do not like doing, which means it is probably the right move. I have been looking over the line for two ticks. This tick I am stepping over it, carefully, with one foot, ready to step back if the signal reverses.
